old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-0adq","title":"Broadcast relay rate-limit keyed on sender IID has no extraction path under upstream addressing","description":"Edge-case review finding from project-LICHEN-worker6-9hnr. spec/04-network.md §6.3.3 keys broadcast relay state on the original sender's IID (line 138 'sender_iid: \u003cIID of original sender\u003e'; line 159 'sender = packet.source_iid'). After the upstream-yggdrasil-addressing reconciliation (§6.2), a relayed broadcast's primary source address bit-packs the inverted Ed25519 key and contains no IID, and the link-layer SIID is an unauthenticated per-hop hint that is never an IPv6 IID (spec/02-physical-link.md:201). No field of a relayed broadcast yields the original sender's IID, so the rate-limit pseudocode has no defined key extraction path. Fix options: key the relay budget on the full 16-byte primary source address (simplest; same binding strength), or define an authenticated field that carries the origin IID end-to-end.
